brief: Meta's Muse app hit No. 1 on the U.S. iPhone free chart, which the market read as confirming mass-agent adoption needs CPU, RAM and storage capacity: ARM +17%, Intel +12%, AMD +10%, Nasdaq +2.3%, SOX +4.3%, though participation was uneven (Kospi faded, TSMC down). Privorotsky says this is not a monolithic buy-everything-AI trade: inference differs from frontier training but broadens infrastructure demand past CPUs to memory, storage, networking and power. His framework is rails vs interfaces: agents destroy value in human-facing interfaces (comparison sites, affiliates, subscription shopping) while creating rail activity (booking, payments, custody, settlement), so friction-dependent businesses look challenged while whoever owns the default agent, he flags Meta, gains outsized distribution value; he expects the labor effect as fewer incremental hires, not mass firing. Separately, oil fell and the curve bull-flattened, but the front end barely moved (2Y -0.8bp vs 10Y -2.9bp) despite falling energy-linked inflation expectations, which he attributes to strong nominal growth or issuance/hyperscaler supply; a genuine front/belly-energy divergence would signal overheating. Iran talks continue without breakthrough; he stays cautiously optimistic on a deal. He trimmed some NDX exposure into yesterday's FOMO rip but stays constructive, preferring bottlenecks, rails and proprietary data over friction-rent businesses.
